notes: §1985:XI.4.2.3 SR2: "A RELEASE statement may be used only within the range of an input procedure associated with a SORT statement for the file-name whose sort-merge file description entry contains record-name-1." GateReleaseReturnRange (below 2002) seeds ProcedureReach.Closure with the input procedures of SORTs naming the file and reports COBOL7081 outside; since kb/Work PB5572 landed a declarative RELEASE is refused where no input procedure for the file exists (pb5572-release-in-declarative-no-input-procedure-85). Re-read 2026-11-15 (registrar landing records-1985-reread, main 2722570af0; logs op-20261115/registrar-1985-reread/log-fmt.txt, log-misc.txt, log-witnesses.txt): RELEASE in the input procedure and in a PERFORMed paragraph of it runs (work-b RL1 AAA ZZZ, refute-b t8 QQQ), a GLOBAL SD record is accepted and a contained program may MOVE into it (t10, t11); RELEASE in the main line after the SORT and of another SD's record is refused COBOL7081 (RL2, t7). kb/Work PB5628 (landed, wave 20262045): the range crosses a CALL (§1985:XI.4.4.4 GR7, "all statements that are executed as the result of a transfer of control by CALL"): VersionConformancePass.CalledFromRange computes, once per compilation group, the programs a CALL in a range activates, and GateReleaseReturnRange accepts their RELEASE; StatementValidation.ResolveRecordName resolves a contained program's GLOBAL record of a non-GLOBAL SD or FD to that file at 85 (the containing-program rule begins at 2002, §2002:13.16.25.2 SR3). work-b/r9.cob prints GGG at --std 85 on the PB5569/PB5575 branch merged with main (06574c173c; E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/finish-w20262057a/runs/r9-001); witnesses pb5628_release_in_called_contained_program_85 and its refusal pb5628-release-in-contained-program-outside-range-85 (a REFUSED SORT's procedures are skipped too, kb/Work PB5496). kb/Work PB5768 (wave 20262068): the declarative RELEASE was exempted wholesale once any procedure existed, although GR7/GR10 admit only declaratives executed as a result of the range's statements; VersionConformancePass.DeclarativeExecutableFromRange now exempts a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR procedure's statement only when the range holds an input-output statement on a file the USE names (any file for an open-mode USE) or a CALL, so refute-b/t14 (a range with neither) is refused COBOL7081 (witness pb5768-release-in-declarative-not-executable-from-range-85) and pb5572_release_in_declarative_of_input_procedure_85 still runs.

next.reason: 1985 states as a syntax rule that 'A RELEASE statement may be used only within the range of an input procedure associated with a SORT statement' for its file, so a violating program is refused. 2023 has no such syntax rule (14.9.32.3 SR1-4 carry none); §2023:14.9.32.4 GR1 says it 'may be executed only' there and 'If it is executed at any other time, the EC-FLOW-RELEASE exception condition is set to exist', and §2023:14.9.40.4 GR13 sets EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE when an output procedure's range executes a RELEASE. A compile-time refusal became a run-time exception condition.
